answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited, stake-weighted task market: agents must lock scarce tokens before bidding, and a randomly selected verifier releases payment only after checking the work against a hidden test. A new identity gets no extra influence because its bids still require separate locked stake, while failed or collusive bids forfeit part of it. So an attacker can mint names cheaply, but scaling a sybil swarm ties up capital and risks losing it. Jade, dune, and violet can be harmless agent names; none substitutes for stake or verified work.
